The test image shows a close-up of plant tissue (likely a stem or pod) with:
- White/grayish cottony mycelium covering the surface
- Small black dots scattered across the tissue (pycnidia or sclerotia)
- Bleached/pale tan underlying tissue

Top candidates: **White Mold** (cottony mycelium + sclerotia) or **Diaporthe/Phomopsis** (pycnidia on bleached stem). Let me check reference images.

**Analysis:**

- **Test image**: Close-up of plant stem/pod tissue covered in dense white/grayish cottony mycelium with scattered small black dots embedded in or on the tissue surface. The underlying tissue is bleached/straw-colored.

- **White Mold** reference: Shows fluffy white cottony mycelium (Sclerotinia sclerotiorum) on bleached stem/pod tissue — matches the cottony texture and bleached appearance very well.

- **Diaporthe**: Shows darkened/bleached stems with canker lesions, no cottony mycelium — doesn't match.

- **Phomopsis**: Shows pod rot with circular dark lesions on pods — doesn't match the cottony appearance.

The white cottony mycelium on bleached tissue is the hallmark of **White Mold** (Sclerotinia sclerotiorum). The small black dots are consistent with sclerotia embedded in the mycelial mat.
